title: Enterprise Coding Assistant
subtitle: Complete private-repository code with bounded context, scoped caches, task routing and validated output.
theme: Agents and Copilots in Real Workflows
author: By Sourav Banerjee

practice_prompts.label: Constraints and discovery
practice_prompts.hint: Which answers set the 300 ms budget, the context scope and the privacy boundary?

practice_prompts.label: Trace a keystroke
practice_prompts.hint: Follow a cache hit and a miss from extension to editor, naming each permission check.

practice_prompts.label: Failures and the cost pivot
practice_prompts.hint: Which failures go silent, which fail closed, and what do you measure when the bill rises?

practice_prompts.label: Evaluation and rollout
practice_prompts.hint: What proves productivity and zero leaks before you add the next repository?

rubric: States the 300 ms p95 and the private-repository boundary before drawing components.
Places the permission-scoped completion cache before embedding, retrieval and the model, and still validates hits.
Narrows context through a funnel and keys retrieval to code-host ACLs checked at indexing and again at retrieval.
Routes by declared IDE task: small model for inline completion, larger model on an isolated slow lane.
Validates syntax, APIs against the symbol index, secrets, licence and unsafe patterns, and stays silent when validation is unavailable.
Adds 10 + 40 + 200 + 50, notes there is no headroom and separates first token from full completion.
Proves value with acceptance slices plus a matched-control productivity comparison, and gates release on zero leaks.
Answers the cost pivot by measuring input and output tokens before changing models.

editorial_review.evidence: 16 Nov 2026: re-read all 51 captured sections against the earlier teach-mode draft section by section. The draft had omitted the intern Alex keystroke trace, the seven-question discovery table, the six functional requirements and interview shortcut, the eight-step architecture list, the 'what gets cached' and semantic-invalidation points, the 'ignore previous instructions' injection example, the two-minute answer, three-sentence close, eight carry lines and six weak-answer repairs; all are restored. Telegraphic draft prose was rewritten into full sentences with terms (ghost text, ACL, p95, MoSCoW, SLO, CDN) defined on first use. Figure captions and alt text were rewritten from each SVG's actual labels; inspecting the hot-path lane showed its cache hit bypasses validation. Follow-ups that duplicated Check Yourself were merged into those answers and the rest became reveals; added illustrative values and our own cautions are labelled. Coverage now has 64 rows with section-specific evidence. Source inconsistencies resolved in text (2026-11-16): hot-path figure's cache hit going straight to the editor vs the text's hit-to-validation rule → validation on every path, because the text, the compact and wide figures and the Check Yourself answer all route hits through validation; the figure stays unedited and its caption says in one neutral sentence what it leaves out. Original vertical figure's hit rejoining the prompt builder → caption states the design (hit skips the model, goes to validation); correction meta-paragraph removed. Stream-before-validate tension → nothing shown before validation passes (buffer or incremental validation); the 'our note, not the source's' label removed.
